topic: The Sun and the geomagnetic field (G3A; 14 pool questions)

questions.question: How does a higher sunspot number affect HF propagation?

choices.A: Higher sunspot numbers generally indicate a greater probability of good propagation at higher frequencies
choices.B: Lower sunspot numbers generally indicate greater probability of sporadic E propagation
choices.C: A zero sunspot number indicates that radio propagation is not possible on any band
choices.D: A zero sunspot number indicates undisturbed conditions

questions.answer: Higher sunspot numbers generally indicate a greater probability of good propagation at higher frequencies

questions.question: What effect does a sudden ionospheric disturbance have on the daytime ionospheric propagation?

choices.A: It enhances propagation on all HF frequencies
choices.B: It disrupts signals on lower frequencies more than those on higher frequencies
choices.C: It disrupts communications via satellite more than direct communications
choices.D: None, because only areas on the night side of the Earth are affected

questions.answer: It disrupts signals on lower frequencies more than those on higher frequencies

questions.question: Approximately how long does it take the increased ultraviolet and X-ray radiation from a solar flare to affect radio propagation on Earth?
Which of the following are the least reliable bands for long-distance communications during periods of low solar activity?
What is the solar flux index?

choices.A: A measure of the highest frequency that is useful for ionospheric propagation between two points on Earth
choices.B: A count of sunspots that is adjusted for solar emissions
choices.C: Another name for the American sunspot number
choices.D: A measure of solar radiation with a wavelength of 10.7 centimeters

questions.answer: A measure of solar radiation with a wavelength of 10.7 centimeters

questions.question: What is a geomagnetic storm?

choices.A: A sudden drop in the solar flux index
choices.B: A thunderstorm that affects radio propagation
choices.D: A temporary disturbance in Earth’s geomagnetic field

questions.answer: A temporary disturbance in Earth’s geomagnetic field

questions.question: At what point in the solar cycle does the 20-meter band usually support worldwide propagation during daylight hours?
How can a geomagnetic storm affect HF propagation?
How can high geomagnetic activity benefit radio communications?

choices.A: Creates auroras that can reflect VHF signals
choices.B: Increases signal strength for HF signals passing through the polar regions

questions.answer: Creates auroras that can reflect VHF signals

questions.question: What causes HF propagation conditions to vary periodically in a 26- to 28-day cycle?

choices.A: Long term oscillations in the upper atmosphere
choices.B: Cyclic variation in Earth’s radiation belts
choices.C: Rotation of the Sun’s surface layers around its axis
choices.D: The position of the Moon in its orbit

questions.answer: Rotation of the Sun’s surface layers around its axis

questions.question: How long does it take a coronal mass ejection to affect radio propagation on Earth?
What does the K-index measure?

choices.A: The relative position of sunspots on the surface of the Sun
choices.B: The short-term stability of Earth’s geomagnetic field
choices.C: The short-term stability of the Sun’s magnetic field
choices.D: The solar radio flux at Boulder, Colorado

questions.answer: The short-term stability of Earth’s geomagnetic field

questions.question: What does the A-index measure?

choices.A: The relative position of sunspots on the surface of the Sun
choices.B: The amount of polarization of the Sun’s electric field
choices.C: The long-term stability of Earth’s geomagnetic field
choices.D: The solar radio flux at Boulder, Colorado

questions.answer: The long-term stability of Earth’s geomagnetic field
